inputs.source: SSO authenticated employee question in chat

controls.name: Read-only least-privilege credential scoped to policy index
Verified network-layer egress deny except chat reply path
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay with model capability because outbound network destinations are blocked outside the model; only the fixed chat reply path remains reachable.

controls.name: Reply destination bound to authenticated requester chat session
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay with model capability because the destination is fixed by the chat system to the authenticated requester's session rather than chosen by the model.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay with model capability because client-side fetching and rendering behaviors are disabled outside the model.

controls.name: Pinned model with change-ticket requirement for changes
Prompt restricts answers to published HR policies and says to decline legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Prompt-only restrictions rely on model compliance and weaken under stronger models, longer contexts, or purpose drift.

findings.title: Bounded employee-to-policy-answer path with internal-data reply only to the authenticated requester

attack_path.note: Trusted employee question can influence search and final answer.
Agent reads only published internal HR policies.
Agent replies only into the same authenticated requester's chat session.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest diff, widened credential/data-source grants, network policy changes, or reply routing changes that allow destinations beyond the authenticated requester session.

evidence.observation: The only declared tool is policy_search.search, which searches the published HR policy index.
The policy index holds only published policies with internal sensitivity, and the agent credential is read only and scoped to that index.
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session, the client does not auto-fetch links or render images, and network egress is denied at the network layer and verified by pen test.

recommendations.action: Keep reply routing bound to the authenticated requester from the system of record and require review for any change that introduces alternate recipients or outbound channels.

findings.title: Prompt-only scope control could be bypassed if the agent's purpose or model changes, but present capability set keeps impact low

attack_path.note: Trusted employee asks an ambiguous or out-of-scope question.
Agent may still produce an answer directly in chat.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version change, prompt change that broadens purpose beyond published policy QA, rising task length, or addition of tools that let the model act beyond chat reply.

evidence.observation: The prompt limits the agent to published Acme HR policies, instructs it to use policy_search, say when policy does not answer, and not give legal advice.
The agent has no other tools, no memory, and no network egress, which constrains present impact even if the behavioral instruction is imperfect.

recommendations.action: Preserve the narrow one-tool design and require reassessment before adding capabilities that could turn prompt-scope failures into higher-impact actions.

rating.rationale: Manual validation applied against the checklist because scripts could not be run. Present design is narrow: one read-only search capability over internal published policies and one reply path bound to the authenticated requester session, with verified network egress denial and no memory or additional tools. That keeps present inherent and residual risk low. Forecast rises to moderate if a significant change occurs, especially new tools, data-scope expansion, or removal of the destination/egress constraints, because those changes would defeat the structural controls that currently keep the path bounded.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, IaC, or live runtime configuration was provided, so control verification is limited to the statements in the runtime notes except where the notes explicitly say a pen test verified network egress denial.

No chat platform protocol or implementation detail was provided beyond destination binding and no auto-fetch behavior, so session-binding and client rendering protections are assessed as declared design facts rather than independently verified.
